0.0.n: Introduces the starting point before the main explanation.

0.1.n: Names information the speaker wants listeners to keep in mind.

0.2.n: Follows 前提 to frame the next statement as background information.

0.3.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers.

0.4.n: Marks 僕 as the topic of the sentence.

0.5.n: Gives the frequency of the purchase.

0.6.n: Directly describes the iPhone being purchased.

0.8.n: Marks the new iPhone as what the speaker buys.

0.9.n: 購入する becomes polite 購入しています; with 毎年, it describes a regular habit.

1.0.n: Connects this explanation to the preceding background statement.

1.1.n: Refers to the current purchase or discussion.

1.2.n: Marks 今回 as the topic, focusing on this occasion.

1.3.n: The model number in the iPhone series name.

1.4.n: A borrowed English word referring to the lineup of related models.

1.5.n: Links the 17 series to 中, expressing its interior or membership.

1.6.n: Combines with の and で to identify the group being compared.

1.7.n: Marks the series as the range within which the speaker chooses.

1.8.n: Refers to the base model rather than a Pro model.

1.9.n: Connects 標準 to 17, describing which version of the model is meant.

1.10.n: The model number here refers specifically to the standard iPhone 17.

1.11.n: Marks the standard 17 as the model to be chosen.

1.12.n: The intention form of 選ぶ; with と思った, it expresses what the speaker planned to choose.

1.13.n: Marks 選ぼう as the content of the speaker’s thought.

1.14.n: Past form of 思う; 選ぼうと思った expresses a past intention to choose.

1.15.n: The preceding phrase describes what these reasons explain.

1.16.n: Pairs with なります to identify what the upcoming explanation covers.

1.17.n: Polite form of なる, used here to present the topic rather than describe an actual change.

2.0.n: The adverb form of 大きい groups the explanation into major points.

2.1.n: Names the points the speaker is about to explain.

2.2.n: Marks 理由 as the topic being counted.

2.3.n: Combines with つ to form the native Japanese count for two things.

2.4.n: A general counting ending used here for reasons.

2.5.n: Adds a polite ending to the statement about the number of reasons.

2.6.n: Softens the statement and invites the listener to follow along.

3.0.n: Combines with つ and 目 to identify the first item.

3.1.n: The general counting ending in 1つ目.

3.2.n: Added after a count, 目 turns it into a position in a sequence.

3.3.n: Marks the first item as what is being identified.

3.4.n: The ending さ turns 重い, meaning heavy, into a noun naming the quality.

3.5.n: Pairs with なります to identify weight as the first reason.

3.6.n: Polite なる is used here as a presentation-style alternative to です, not to describe becoming.

4.0.n: Sets the initial stage before the speaker changed plans.

4.1.n: Highlights the initial plan in contrast with the later decision.

4.2.n: The model number identifying the iPhone generation.

4.3.n: Links the 17 generation to its Pro version.

4.4.n: A product model name identifying the higher-end iPhone version.

4.5.n: In にする, marks the option someone decides on.

4.6.n: The intention form of する; Proにしよう expresses choosing the Pro.

4.7.n: Part of しようとしていた, which describes an ongoing intention or attempt.

4.8.n: Completes colloquial してたん: していた becomes してた, followed by explanatory ん.

4.9.n: Makes the explanatory んです construction polite.

4.10.n: Introduces a contrast; けども is a slightly fuller version of けど.

5.0.n: A shortened English borrowing used for technical product details.

5.1.n: Combines with スペック to name the announcement of specifications.

5.2.n: Marks the specification announcement as what was made.

5.3.n: The linking form of passive される, from する; 発表がされる means an announcement is made.

5.4.n: Follows a verb’s て-form to show that the next action happened afterward.

5.5.n: Polite past form of やめる; the abandoned Pro purchase is understood from context.

6.0.n: Refers back to the decision not to buy the Pro.

6.1.n: Marks that decision as the topic whose reason is being explained.

6.2.n: The model number forming part of the product name 17 Pro.

6.4.n: The product model name distinguishing this version from the standard 17.

6.5.n: Marks 17 Pro as the thing described as excessively heavy.

6.6.n: Remove い from 重い and add すぎる to express excessive heaviness.

6.7.n: Connects the statement about weight to こと, packaging it as a fact.

6.8.n: Turns the preceding statement into something that can be discovered or understood.

6.9.n: Marks the fact about the weight as what became clear.

6.10.n: Past form of 分かる, describing the speaker’s realization.

6.11.n: Marks the discovery as the reason for abandoning the purchase.

6.12.n: The な plus explanatory ん connects the reason ending in から to です.

6.13.n: Makes the explanation polite as part of なんです.

6.14.n: Emphasizes the explanation as information the speaker wants the listener to notice.

6.15.n: Softens the emphasis of よ and invites shared understanding.

0.lit: First, as a premise, I buy a new iPhone every year.
0.tip: With 毎年, 購入しています describes a repeated habit, not a purchase happening right now.

1.lit: So, this time, these will be the reasons I thought to choose the standard 17 among the 17 series.
1.tip: 選ぼうと思った means the speaker formed an intention to choose, rather than simply having a thought about choosing.

2.lit: Broadly speaking, the reasons are two, you see.
2.tip: 大きく signals that the reasons are being grouped into broad categories.

3.tip: Adding 目 after a count makes an order: 1つ目 means the first item.

4.lit: At first, I was planning to go with the 17 Pro, but…
4.tip: にしようとしてた is casual にしようとしていた, describing what the speaker had been planning to choose.

5.lit: After the specification announcement was made, I gave up on it.
5.tip: A verb’s て-form followed by から means after doing that, not because.

6.lit: That is because I found out the fact that the 17 Pro is too heavy, you see.
6.tip: 重すぎる uses すぎる to mean excessively heavy, not merely very heavy.
